title: SGD Classification
body:
[[Gradient Descent]]

Stochastic gradient descent estimates the gradient from a random minibatch instead of the full
dataset, so each step is an unbiased estimate of the true gradient with a standard error that
shrinks as $1/\sqrt{n}$. That is [[Sampling Distribution]] in [[STATISTICS]], and it is
why small batches still converge. On a linear model with squared error, [[Linear Regression]]
solves the same problem exactly and in closed form, which is [[Optimization]] in [[CALCULUS 1]]
with the derivative set to zero and actually solvable.
